long_biography.plain_text:
Captain Elias Gotsis joined the American Club's board as Eurotankers' representative in 2008. The mutual insurer brings shipowners together to govern protection-and-indemnity cover, extending his industry role beyond management of the family's Piraeus shipping interests. He remained among the club's directors in its 2025 board listing.

At Eurotankers, operating practice centres on long-serving seafarers and office staff, continuous training and close monitoring of each managed ship. The company combines tanker and bulk-carrier operations with commercial and technical departments in Piraeus. Its stated approach favours practical, analytical decisions and adoption of new technology across both fleet and office.

uncertainties.detail: Eurotankers was formed in 1990 and strong sources establish Gotsis as an owner, head and managing director. Public evidence does not reliably identify the founder, starting capital or whether the original family shipping assets were created, acquired or inherited by him, so wealth origin remains Unknown.

Dun & Bradstreet supplies the full name Elias Michail Gotsis for the exact Eurotankers principal. No second primary source publishes the middle name, so the proposed value carries medium rather than high confidence.
Companies House independently confirms March 1946, Greek nationality and Greek residence but does not publish the exact day or birthplace. Those missing fields remain unproposed.

Searches returned a younger Greek fitness personality, a hospitality worker and a psychotherapist with Elias or Ilias Gotsis names. Their ages and occupations conflict with the March 1946 identity and Eurotankers record, so their biographies and social profiles were excluded.
No LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X/Twitter or personal website could be tied to the senior Eurotankers executive with identity confidence at or above 85. Name-only accounts were excluded.
No dedicated Forbes profile or exact Forbes coverage was found after searches for both Elias and Ilias spellings.
All current vessel facts, fleet counts, transaction values, short-lived ownership percentages, controversies and unsupported personal wealth estimates are excluded from the biographies.
